name: Amazon Rainforest (Primary Terra Firme)
reference_source: Saatchi et al. (2011) PNAS; Baccini et al. (2012) Nature Climate Change
notes: Intact core Amazonian terra firme evergreen moist broadleaf rainforest in Amazonas state with continuous high canopy.

name: Congo Basin Forest (Lowland Equatorial)
reference_source: Lewis et al. (2013) Nature; Gourlet-Fleury et al. (2011) Forest Ecology and Management
notes: Central equatorial Congo Basin dense evergreen forest with structural complexity and high carbon density.

name: Borneo Dipterocarp Rainforest
reference_source: Slik et al. (2013) Global Ecology and Biogeography; Langner et al. (2007)
notes: Ancient primary lowland Dipterocarpaceae forest characterized by emergent trees exceeding 50m height.

name: Black Forest (Schwarzwald)
reference_source: Thurner et al. (2014) Global Ecology and Biogeography; German National Forest Inventory (BWI3)
notes: Montane mixed temperate forest dominated by silver fir (Abies alba), Norway spruce, and European beech.

name: Redwood National and State Parks
reference_source: Van Pelt et al. (2016) Forest Ecology and Management; Busing & Fujimori (2005)
notes: Coastal temperate rainforest supporting the tallest living trees on Earth with immense biomass per hectare.

name: Finnish Boreal Taiga (Kainuu)
reference_source: Thurner et al. (2014); Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke) NFI
notes: Mid-boreal coniferous forest dominated by Pinus sylvestris and Picea abies adapted to short growing seasons.

name: Central Siberian Taiga
reference_source: Schepaschenko et al. (2011) Biomass and Bioenergy; Houghton et al. (2007)
notes: Continuous Siberian boreal needleleaf forest on continuous permafrost with cold-climate slow biomass accumulation.

name: Sundarbans Mangrove Delta
reference_source: Simard et al. (2019) Nature Geoscience; Giri et al. (2008)
notes: World's largest contiguous halophytic mangrove forest delta, dominated by Heritiera fomes (Sundari).

name: Western Ghats Wet Evergreen Forest
reference_source: Ramesh et al. (2010); Forest Survey of India (FSI) 2021
notes: Biodiversity hotspot tropical wet evergreen montane forest in the Anamalai Hills of southern India.

name: Yasuní National Park
reference_source: Valencia et al. (2004); Bass et al. (2010) PLoS ONE
notes: High-diversity western Amazonian moist equatorial rainforest near the intersection of the Andes and Amazon.

name: Sahara Desert (Erg Chech)
reference_source: Dynamic World Bare Ground / ESA WorldCover 2021 baseline
notes: Hyper-arid Saharan sand dune field demonstrating CanopyAI zero-biomass edge-case detection.

name: Pacific Ocean (Equatorial Pelagic)
reference_source: Copernicus Marine / GEBCO Open Pelagic Ocean baseline
notes: Open pelagic ocean surface demonstrating water detection, zero carbon stock, and low confidence.

name: Deforested Amazon Patch (Arc of Deforestation)
reference_source: INPE PRODES Deforestation Monitoring / Hansen Global Forest Change
notes: Post-deforestation pasture and secondary scrub in northern Mato Grosso exhibiting severe canopy loss.
